hints: There are 9 people in total to be divided into two groups of sizes 6 and 3.
Choosing the 6 people for the first group automatically leaves the remaining 3 people for the other group.
walkthrough:
Calculate the number of ways to choose 6 people from 9 (which automatically determines the group of 3):
$$\text{Number of ways} = \binom{9}{6} = \binom{9}{3} = \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 84$$
teacher_walkthrough: There are 9 people in total (4 in the Ahmed family and 5 in the Baker family).
We want to find the number of ways to divide the 9 people into a group of 6 and a group of 3.

Step 1: Apply combinations.
Choosing 6 people out of 9 leaves the remaining 3 people to form the second group:
$$\binom{9}{6} = \frac{9!}{6! \, 3!} = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 84$$

Equivalently, choosing 3 people out of 9 to form the smaller group leaves the remaining 6 people:
$$\binom{9}{3} = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 84$$
Thus, there are 84 ways.

hints: 5 of the 9 people are selected at random. Calculate the total number of selections: $\binom{9}{5} = 126$.
To include all 3 Baker children, those 3 children are fixed in the selection.
Choose the remaining $5 - 3 = 2$ people from the remaining $9 - 3 = 6$ people: $\binom{6}{2} = 15$.
Divide favorable selections by total selections: $\dfrac{15}{126} = \dfrac{5}{42}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total number of ways to choose 5 people from 9:
$$\text{Total selections} = \binom{9}{5} = \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 126$$

Calculate the number of selections containing all 3 Baker children:
All 3 Baker children are included, leaving 2 people to be chosen from the other 6 people:
$$\text{Favorable selections} = \binom{3}{3} \times \binom{6}{2} = 1 \times 15 = 15$$

ai_rubric.Finding Probability by Counting: Calculates favorable selections 6C2 = 15 and total selections 9C5 = 126 to obtain 5/42 or 0.119.

teacher_walkthrough: 5 people are selected at random from the 9 people. We want the probability that the group contains all 3 of the Baker children.

Step 1: Calculate the total number of possible groups of 5:
$$\binom{9}{5} = \frac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 126$$

Step 2: Calculate the number of favorable groups.
All 3 Baker children must be in the group. This leaves:
$$5 - 3 = 2 \text{ spots to fill}$$
These 2 people must be chosen from the remaining $9 - 3 = 6$ people (Mr & Mrs Baker, Mr & Mrs Ahmed, and the 2 Ahmed children):
$$\binom{6}{2} = \frac{6 \times 5}{2 \times 1} = 15$$

Step 3: Compute the probability:
$$\mathrm{P} = \frac{15}{126}$$
Divide numerator and denominator by 3:
$$\frac{15 \div 3}{126 \div 3} = \frac{5}{42}$$
In decimal form:
$$\frac{5}{42} \approx 0.119047... \approx 0.119$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.119$.

hints: Use the subtraction method: total arrangements of 9 people minus arrangements where Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker are standing next to each other.
Total unrestricted arrangements of 9 people in a line is $9! = 362\,880$.
Treat Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker as a single block: $(AB)$, which can be ordered in $2!$ ways. The block plus the other 7 people gives 8 items, arranged in $8!$ ways: $8! \times 2! = 80\,640$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total number of unrestricted arrangements of 9 people in a line:
$$\text{Total arrangements} = 9! = 362\,880$$

Calculate the arrangements where Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker are together:
$$\text{Treat } (AB) \text{ as 1 unit}: \quad 8! \times 2! = 40\,320 \times 2 = 80\,640$$

Subtract to find the arrangements where they are not next to each other:
$$\text{Required arrangements} = 9! - (8! \times 2!) = 362\,880 - 80\,640 = 282\,240$$

Alternative Method (Gap insertion):
$$\text{Arrange the other 7 people} = 7! = 5040$$
$$\text{Place Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker into 2 of the 8 available spaces} = 8 \times 7 = 56$$
$$\text{Total} = 5040 \times 56 = 282\,240$$
teacher_walkthrough: All 9 people stand in a line. We want to find the number of arrangements in which Mr Ahmed is not standing next to Mr Baker.

Step 1: Total number of arrangements of 9 distinct people:
$$\text{Total} = 9! = 362\,880$$

Step 2: Number of arrangements where Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker ARE together.
Treat Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker as a single block: $(A, B)$.
There are 2 ways to order them within the block: $AB$ or $BA$.
The block together with the remaining 7 people gives 8 items to arrange:
$$\text{Together arrangements} = 8! \times 2! = 40\,320 \times 2 = 80\,640$$

Step 3: Subtract the forbidden arrangements:
$$\text{Valid arrangements} = 362\,880 - 80\,640 = 282\,240$$

Method 2: Gap insertion method.
First arrange the other 7 people in a line: $7! = 5040$ ways.
This line creates $7 + 1 = 8$ gaps (including the two ends).
Place Mr Ahmed in one gap (8 choices) and Mr Baker in a different gap (7 choices):
$$\text{Valid arrangements} = 7! \times 8 \times 7 = 5040 \times 56 = 282\,240$$

hints: Exactly one person must stand between Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker, creating a 3-person block $[A, P, B]$ or $[B, P, A]$.
Choose which of the other 7 people stands between them: 7 choices.
Account for the two internal orders of Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker: 2 ways.
Treat the 3-person block as 1 item, which together with the remaining 6 people gives 7 items to arrange in $7!$ ways: $7 \times 2 \times 7!$.
walkthrough:
Form a 3-person unit consisting of Mr Ahmed, one intervening person, and Mr Baker:
$$\text{Choices for the intervening person from the other 7 people} = 7$$
$$\text{Internal arrangements of Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker} (A-P-B \text{ or } B-P-A) = 2$$

Treat this triplet as 1 combined unit. Arrange this unit alongside the remaining 6 people ($1 + 6 = 7$ units in total):
$$\text{Arrangements of 7 units} = 7! = 5040$$

Calculate the total number of arrangements:
$$\text{Total} = 7 \times 2 \times 7! = 14 \times 5040 = 70\,560$$
teacher_walkthrough: All 9 people stand in a line. We want to find the number of arrangements in which there is exactly one person standing between Mr Ahmed and Mr Baker.

Step 1: Construct the sandwich unit.
The unit consists of Mr Ahmed ($A$), one chosen person ($P$), and Mr Baker ($B$):
$$[A, P, B] \quad \text{or} \quad [B, P, A]$$
- Choice of person $P$:
There are 7 other people in the group, so there are $7$ options for $P$.
- Order of $A$ and $B$:
$A$ and $B$ can be placed on either side of $P$ in $2$ ways.

Step 2: Treat the sandwich $[A, P, B]$ as a single block.
After selecting $P$, there are $9 - 3 = 6$ other people remaining.
We now arrange the block and the 6 other people:
$$\text{Number of units to arrange} = 1 + 6 = 7 \text{ units}$$
These 7 units can be arranged in $7!$ ways:
$$7! = 5040$$

Step 3: Multiply the choices at each stage:
$$\text{Total arrangements} = 7 \times 2 \times 7! = 14 \times 5040 = 70\,560$$
Thus, there are 70560 valid arrangements.
